subject: SIG / CAIQ sequencing and control-sampling intake — clarifying owners & windows
messages:
From: Morgan Ellis <m.ellis@audita.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ sequencing questions ahead of ISO scoping

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the intake call earlier. Before we finalize the audit scope for Acadia’s review, a couple of clarifying questions on sequencing and evidence windows so we can size sampling properly: 

1) Do you expect us to consume your SIG/CAIQ export first and then accept ISO Annex mapping afterward, or would you prefer we map high-risk SIG controls into ISO controls up-front (we typically prefer the former but can flex)?

2) For control-sampling windows: are you planning a rolling 6-month sample or a single contiguous 90-day window for the first audit? Any retention cutoffs we should be aware of (esp. for KV/cache backups)?

3) Evidence ownership: can you provide a point person for encryption/KMS evidence, and a separate owner for network access logs (we need direct contacts who can pull artifacts quickly during intake)?

If you can attach your latest SIG export and an intake owner list, we’ll draft the sample plan and share a proposed timeline.

Best,
Morgan
Senior Engagement Lead, Audita

---

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ sequencing questions ahead of ISO scoping

Morgan —

Appreciate the questions. Short answers up-front, then proposed approach: 

1) Sequencing: we prefer a phased intake. Please ingest the SIG/CAIQ export first so you can identify high-risk control families. We will provide an ISO Annex mapping deliverable in parallel, but we want you to have the canonical SIG CSV to drive initial sampling.

2) Sampling window: for the inaugural audit we want a 90-day contiguous window (Q1 -> Q2 slice). That keeps the engineering pull manageable and aligns with our logging retention for production (we retain full logs for 90 days by default; longer retention is archived). If your sample plan requires a 6-month rolling window for certain controls, flag those controls and we'll evaluate extended pulls case-by-case.

3) Evidence owners: see owners below (we'll formalize in the intake template attached):
  - KMS / encryption artifacts: Olga Petrov (olga@redwood.com)
  - Network access logs / WAF: Jonas Weber (jonas@redwood.com)
  - Identity / provisioning: Kimberly Park (kimberly@redwood.com)

I’ve attached our intake-template-v2.xlsx and included a CSV export of the SIG (redwood-sig-export-20270504.csv). We think phased delivery (SIG first, mapping + ISO deliverable within 10 business days) is the least disruptive.

Please confirm if 90 days is OK or whether you need an initial short list for extended retention pulls.

Thanks — Rishi
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sig-export-20270504.csv, intake-template-v2.xlsx

Thanks — quick operational clarifications from infra: 

- KV/cache backups: production KV snapshots are retained for 180 days in cold storage; however, hot access logs are only 90 days. If Audita needs snapshot contents (for example to validate rollback behavior), that will require a scoped SRE ticket and 3 business day lead time.

- Encryption evidence: KMS key rotation logs and key policy snapshots are available; we can export key usage metrics for the 90-day window but rotation history beyond 1 year is archived.

I’m attaching a small diagram that shows where the artifacts live (infra-kv-diagram.png). For anything outside the 90-day hot window, please annotate the controls and we’ll triage.

— Olga
